model.definition: planar_transform<Native> in native/affine_transform.h returns PlanarTransform{collapsed, factors}: collapsed when affine_factors returns nullopt (a singular matrix, by the same exact detection as before: zero magnitude, or proportional columns by the product test that avoids a false nonzero determinant after normalization) or when a scale factor rounds to zero in Native (godot::real_t); rounds_to_zero compares with half the smallest subnormal, so no conversion can overflow; a default PlanarTransform is the identity
model.visibility: ApplicationRuntime::apply resolves the transform once per View, stores it with the committed shadow and decides visible = displayType != None && !collapsed, the one place a View's visibility is decided; the existing rule for hidden Controls cancels the contacts of the subtree
model.kept: A collapsed Control keeps the last invertible transform it carried: apply_transform returns early, so its geometry stays finite until a later update brings an invertible transform; the native driver's synchronous updates go through the same apply

oracle.independence: Derives, from the JSX declaration and with plain arithmetic, the box RN computes for each degenerate matrix (the bounding box of the four corners mapped about the center), the planar matrix of every shown state, the press points and the plate-local point, the offsets of the captured gesture and the pixel each sample must show, and never reads the probe's pass flags: a report with every flag forced to passed is still rejected when a recorded Control, frame, press or event is wrong or missing. For the float rank-loss case it checks on its own that the matrix is not singular and that its smaller singular value rounds to zero in Math.fround.

every visible Godot error is a failed check or a host error the report keeps

capture.why: RN's retargeter subtracts the origin of the capture owner's transformed box from the client point (PointerEventsProcessor.cpp, retargetPointerEvent); for scale: 0 that box is the point at the owner's center, (108, 190), so (160, 260) gives (52, 70)

focus.meaning: exit/FOCUS_RELEASED asserts it: before the animation the field has the focus (JS saw focus); after the collapse Godot has no focus owner and JS saw focus then blur

departures: A touch in progress inside a collapsed View is canceled (RN keeps it): a Control that is not visible takes no input, as for every hidden subtree; keeping the contact would need a guarded projection through a singular transform, which Godot does not represent (Control.scale is never zero).

Keyboard focus inside a collapsed View: a collapse through the native driver releases it (Godot's hide; asserted by exit/FOCUS_RELEASED), a collapse through a React commit keeps it because the host's transaction restores the focus owner at its end, as it already does for display: none (an exploratory observation, not asserted); RN keeps the focus in both. A guard on is_visible_in_tree() in that restoration would make the two paths agree and is an open item.

iOS refuses hits below a determinant of 1e-6 (a scale of about 1e-3) and Android treats a 3x3 determinant below 1e-5 as singular; the host collapses only where RN's own flattening makes the matrix exactly singular or the scale rounds to zero in a float, so between 1e-5 and 1e-3 it shows a Control smaller than a pixel.
A collapsed capture owner receives RN's own payload (the client point minus the origin of its transformed box), not coordinates projected through the Control: the same precedent as display none.
exploratoryObservationsOutsideTheReceipt: In a scratch experiment with a text field inside a View collapsed by React state, the LineEdit kept the focus and JS saw focus, blur and focus: Godot's hide released it and the transaction's focus restoration returned it (not retained).

The runner rejected a sabotage receipt with a tampered host hash ('The receipt is not about the host under test') and one with a tampered source hash ('is not the source the sabotage ran against'), and accepted the restored original again.

In an earlier run the Control collapsed and returned within the first frames of the native-driver ease; the oracle accepts this because a frame is never shown below RN's zero nor hidden once the scale is clearly away from it.

Control.set_scale(Vector2.ZERO) leaves (1e-05, 1e-05), and Transform2D.affine_inverse of a singular transform prints 'Condition "det == 0" is true' in the editor binary the lanes use (two scratch scripts, not retained).

The SDK and adapter steps refuse an output directory that exists and the prior receipts keep theirs in build/, so they ran with the same commands and fresh directories (see sdkAndAdapters).

sdkAndAdapters.outputDirectories: fresh build/*-ca9f195 directories for codegen-native-compile, native-sdk, adapter-registry, adapter-loader and adapter-runtime; test:consumer, test:cold and parity:godot used their own

limits: 3D, perspective, rotateX/rotateY (every z-coupling entry), a weight other than 1 and transformOrigin z remain rejected; the public rejection cases are six (61 checks) since singular and rank-one became positive cases.

Touches in progress inside a collapsed View are canceled where RN keeps them, and keyboard focus is released by a native-driver collapse but kept by a React-commit one (the host's transaction restores the focus owner, as for display: none), where RN keeps it in both; a guard on is_visible_in_tree() in that restoration, and a real zero scale with a guarded projection that would keep touches and focus, are open items.

iOS refuses hits below a determinant of 1e-6 and Android treats a 3x3 determinant below 1e-5 as singular; the host collapses only at an exactly singular matrix or a scale that rounds to zero in a float.
The scene presses with the mouse; touch input on a collapsed or restored Pressable, a collapse under a ScrollView, transformed clipping, scaleZ and Godot Android and iOS exports are not covered.

The animated frame counts and the number of visibility changes in the first frames of the ease vary with the frame rate; the checks assert order, bounds and the planar matrix of every shown frame, not those counts.

test:animated failed once in the battery on an oracle timing check of the JS driver (2 ms tolerance) and passed on three reruns; the SDK and adapter steps refuse an output directory that exists and ran again in fresh ones; every other native-cold-start step passed on its first run.
No whole GF, checkpoint, dependency, weight or denominator closed: GF-10 is not at its first slice, so its slice checkpoint, already closed, does not change.
